sentences.text:
12 July, 2024
 The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender
 Criminal Revision Case No.1431 Of 2013
Order:

The revision petitioner was convicted by the trial Court for the offence under Section 7(i), 2(ia) (j)
and Section 16(1- A)(i) and Rules 23 and 29 of the Prevention of Food Act, 1954 and Rules 1955 and sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of three months.

entities.text: Prevention of Food Act, 1954 and Rules 1955
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The learned Additional District and Sessions in appeal confirmed the said sentence and dismissed the appeal.
Aggrieved by the same, present revision is filed.

2. Heard learned counsel for the revision petitioner and learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for the respondent-State.
3.
The case of the Food Inspector who was examined as PW1 is that he went to the premises of petitioner's shop who is the Proprietor of Gopalanath Kiranam.
He secured the presence of independent mediator who was examined as PW3 and purchased 1500 grams of green gram dal and sealed the said dal by separating into three equal parts.
Proceedings were drafted under Ex.P7.
Thereafter, the sample was sent for the purpose of analysis.
Analyst report was received informing that the sample contained synthetic colour, as such, it was adulterated.
4. Notice was given by the Food Inspector to the accused and thereafter complaint was filed.
5. The learned Magistrate having examined PWs.1 to 3 of whom PW1 is the Food Inspector, found favour with the prosecution that the item was adulterated.
The prosecution also brought on record Exs.P1 to P26.

Having gone through the record, the Food Inspector had followed due procedure while sending the samples to the analyst and also it was informed subsequently to the petitioner regarding adulteration found.
6. The Court below concluded that the food item which is green gram dal kept for sale and human consumption, contained synthetic colour which is harmful to the person who consumes it.
7. I do not find any infirmity with the findings of the Courts below.

However, keeping in view that the incident is of the year 2006 and there are no other cases pending against the revision petitioner which fact is not disputed by the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor, the sentence of imprisonment of the revision petitioner can be reduced to the period already undergone.
8. Accordingly, Criminal Revision Case is partly allowed.
As a sequel, miscellaneous applications, if any, pending shall stand closed.
